attempts.summary: Set up centralized log forwarding from node2's "inventory" application to node1. Created a simulated inventory app (systemd service inventory.service on node2 emitting periodic log lines via logger -t inventory -p local5.info). Configured rsyslog on node2 to forward programname=='inventory' messages via TCP to node1:514 using a disk-assisted (linkedList, saveOnShutdown) queue for resilience. Configured rsyslog on node1 with an imtcp listener on port 514 bound to a dedicated ruleset that writes matching inventory messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log. Opened firewalld TCP/514 on node1. Verified live flow end-to-end, then restarted node2 (log source) and confirmed automatic recovery of both services and resumed forwarding, and restarted node1 (collector) while node2 continued producing logs, confirming node2's disk queue buffered messages during the outage and flushed them to node1's log file once node1 came back up -- demonstrating the flow survives restarts of either system. Both rsyslog services and inventory.service are systemd-enabled for boot persistence. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for both nodes, capturing boot_id before/after each restart as proof of restart, plus post-restart service/data recovery evidence.
